items.title: Systemic `# type: ignore[no-redef]` shadow-patch pattern across app/ -- final re-audit confirms zero remaining genuine dead shadows
items.severity_reasoning: Same P2 reasoning class as TD-CAND-001/002 (recurring instances of the same accidental-duplication risk pattern that produced TD-008's P1 break), now fully evidence-backed rather than a triage placeholder. Re-verified 2026-08-19 at HEAD 0d8c8da: `grep -rl "no-redef" app/` still returns exactly 17 files (unchanged). All 17 -- not 3 -- were individually read this pass. Result: 8 files show a genuine accidental/legacy shadow-redefinition of the TD-CAND-001 kind (a second `def <name>` silently overrides an earlier, unrelated one in the same scope) -- account_visibility_helpers.py (=TD-CAND-001, tracked there, not double-counted here), route_support.py, app/services/menu_visibility.py (both previously verified), plus four newly-verified this pass: app/api/mobile/domains/kpi_target_management.py (3 separate shadow pairs in one file), app/schema_guard_engine.py, app/services/home_dashboard_service.py, app/view_helpers.py. One file, app/services/role_matrix_ui_service.py, uses a DIFFERENT and distinctly fragile pattern -- deliberate sequential monkey-patch layering (each redefinition captures and calls through to the prior definition via a `_PREVIOUS_...` module global before adding its own behavior) -- functionally live, not dead code, but ordering-dependent and easily mistaken for TD-CAND-001-style dead duplication by a future maintainer who does not read the capture-and-delegate lines carefully, which is its own real risk. The remaining 9 files are confirmed LEGITIMATE, not debt: 5 use a `try: from .module import X / except ImportError: from module import X  # type: ignore[no-redef]` fallback pattern for supporting both package-relative and flat-namespace execution contexts (app/services/analytics_center/{dashboard_surface,communication_support_insights,personnel_performance_insights,summary_pipeline,survey_feedback_insights}.py), 1 uses the same fallback pattern for a typed stub class (app/services/personnel/workflow.py), 1 uses the same fallback pattern for a deferred model import (app/services/performance/common.py), and 2 use a deliberate caching-wrapper idiom that captures the original function before shadowing it with a cached version (app/main_handlers/dashboard_handlers.py, app/performance/v2_routes.py) -- structurally identical in spirit to role_matrix_ui_service.py's pattern but simpler (single wrap, not a chain) and not flagged as a separate risk.

items.description: Fresh complete re-audit (2026-08-21, HEAD 80810c42db31917d570ae1079e2dbb47bf8defb0) of every current `# type: ignore[no-redef]` occurrence in app/ (16 occurrences across 14 files) individually classified each remaining case as INTENTIONAL_RUNTIME_LAYERING (5 occurrences / 4 files), COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER / caching-wrapper (3 occurrences / 3 files), or LEGITIMATE_FALLBACK import-compatibility pattern (8 occurrences / 7 files). Wave 1 (commit 187333f785284b004d23e3bed8ea010bd57a96a7) had already removed the only two proven genuine dead shadows, in app/services/menu_visibility.py and app/api/mobile/domains/kpi_target_management.py (21 occurrences/16 files -> 16 occurrences/14 files). evidence: 2026-08-19 (HEAD 0d8c8da) prior evidence, SUPERSEDED by this re-audit: claimed 17 files / 8 genuine-duplication files including route_support.py, schema_guard_engine.py, home_dashboard_service.py, view_helpers.py as accidental shadow-duplication (TD-CAND-001-class). That evidence was built on a file-count metric conflated with a separately-tracked item (account_visibility_helpers.py, TD-CAND-001) and, per the TD-CAND-003 Wave 1 fresh forensic, mischaracterized 4 of those files -- each is actually a deliberate capture-and-delegate pattern (INTENTIONAL_RUNTIME_LAYERING or COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER), not dead code. Preserved here for auditability, not as current fact.

TD-CAND-003 Wave 1 (2026-08-20/21, commit 187333f785284b004d23e3bed8ea010bd57a96a7, parent 334247b893b1fa92252d7040088c6a74fb477b41): fresh forensic across all then-existing no-redef occurrences found 21 occurrences / 16 files. Confirmed exactly 2 files (app/services/menu_visibility.py: _bys360_assistant_apply_key, _bys360_assistant_collect_from_db; app/api/mobile/domains/kpi_target_management.py: 3 legacy wrapper pairs) had genuinely dead, unreachable earlier definitions with no capture/delegate mechanism -- these were deleted (behavior-locked first via 20 new tests in tests/quality/test_menu_visibility_assistant_apply_key_behavior_contract.py, verified via deliberate mutation-sensitivity proof). Also corrected the 2026-08-19 evidence for route_support.py (:507 captures the original build_menu_visibility_map into _BYS360_V13_ORIGINAL_BUILD_MENU_VISIBILITY_MAP, :525 delegates to it -- 1 pair, INTENTIONAL_RUNTIME_LAYERING, not the multi-pair accidental duplication previously claimed), schema_guard_engine.py, view_helpers.py (both same capture-and-delegate pattern), and home_dashboard_service.py (caching-wrapper capture at :217, not accidental duplication). Result: 21->16 occurrences, 16->14 files.

This final re-audit (2026-08-21, HEAD 80810c42db31917d570ae1079e2dbb47bf8defb0): fresh grep for 'type: ignore[no-redef]' confirms exactly 16 occurrences / 14 files (unchanged since Wave 1, proving no new suppressions were introduced). Every occurrence individually read and classified with direct source-level reachability/fallback proof (not inference from comments alone):

INTENTIONAL_RUNTIME_LAYERING (5 occurrences / 4 files) -- each captures the immediately-prior definition into a module-level variable before redefining, and the new definition unconditionally calls through to the captured original: app/route_support.py:525 (captures :404 via _BYS360_V13_ORIGINAL_BUILD_MENU_VISIBILITY_MAP at :507, delegates at :526), app/schema_guard_engine.py:264 (captures the prior should_auto_repair_schema via _BYS360_V13_ORIGINAL_SHOULD_AUTO_REPAIR_SCHEMA at :254, delegates at :266/:269), app/view_helpers.py:148 (captures via _BYS360_PHASE3_6_ORIGINAL_BUILD_SURFACE_SCOPE_CONTEXT at :145, delegates at :149), app/services/role_matrix_ui_service.py:550 and :731 (a genuine 3-layer chain: base _build_role_matrix_ui_context_base at :340 -> layer1 at :425 -> layer2 [:550, this item's first occurrence] captures layer1 at :548 and delegates at :551 -> layer3 [:731, this item's second occurrence] captures layer2 dynamically via globals().get(...) at :730 and delegates at :733, guarded by callable() with a safe {} fallback). Confirmed via grep that every live external caller (app/admin/role_matrix_routes.py:22, tests/security/test_csp_wave4_admin_contract.py:226) calls the exported symbol positionally, so the parameter-name drift across layers (active_group_key vs selected_module) never surfaces as a defect in practice -- flagged as a non-blocking FUTURE_DEBT_CANDIDATE code-smell (see behavior_quirks_to_preserve), not TD-CAND-003 scope.

COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER / caching-wrapper (3 occurrences / 3 files) -- each captures the original uncached implementation into a _..._uncached module variable and wraps it with a short-TTL in-memory cache that always calls through to the original on cache miss or on any exception: app/main_handlers/dashboard_handlers.py:23 (captures the :11 import at :20, calls through at :27/:33), app/performance/v2_routes.py:96 (captures at :64, calls through at :100/:102/:107), app/services/home_dashboard_service.py:220 (captures at :217, calls through at :224).

LEGITIMATE_FALLBACK (8 occurrences / 7 files) -- textbook try/except import-compatibility pattern, mutually-exclusive execution paths, no dead duplicate body: app/services/analytics_center/communication_support_insights.py:11, dashboard_surface.py:12 and :16, personnel_performance_insights.py:12, summary_pipeline.py:22, survey_feedback_insights.py:11 (all: package-relative import in try, flat-namespace analytics_center.*/ai_decision.* import in except ImportError, explicitly supporting a documented standalone 'python -S gate' execution context distinct from normal package import), app/services/performance/common.py:324 (from app.models import User try, from app.models.user import User except, layout-compatibility fallback, returns None gracefully if both fail), app/services/personnel/workflow.py:20 (try imports the real PersonnelFormPayload dataclass from .form_payload; except ImportError/AttributeError defines a minimal safe stand-in dataclass with identical field names/defaults so consumers never hit NameError in a broken-import environment; explicitly pragma: no cover as a break-glass path).

GENUINE_DEAD_SHADOW_COUNT = 0. UNKNOWN_RISK_COUNT = 0. Classification totals (5 INTENTIONAL_RUNTIME_LAYERING + 3 COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER + 8 LEGITIMATE_FALLBACK = 16) match Wave 1's own forward-looking estimate exactly, independently re-derived from fresh source reading rather than copied from that estimate.

The only plausible candidate -- clear_period_task_records(), an admin-gated, manually-triggered bulk-delete, not a hot path -- has 4 single-predicate filter/delete queries, and every column those queries touch already carries adequate index coverage: 3 tables (performance_evaluations, performance_evaluation_items, evaluation_assignments) via composite indexes from migration b4c2d1e9f005 ('add phase5 indexes'); the 4th (assignment_coverage_logs) via a single-column index from migration e6b7d4c2f107, sufficient because its query is single-predicate (a composite index would add zero benefit). Both migrations independently confirmed as ancestors of the current Alembic head (e0efcd07abf7) via a full down_revision-chain traversal of all 74 migration files -- not assumed, traced. No partitioning precedent exists anywhere in this repository's ~75 migrations, and no production evidence (slow-query logs, documented complaints) anywhere supports adding one speculatively. Writing a new migration here would have been unjustified, speculative optimization against an already-adequately-indexed, non-hot-path operation -- the opposite of a minimal, evidence-based fix. Closure action taken: (1) removed the stale comment from app/performance/task_routes.py, (2) added tests/quality/test_td_cand_006_period_evaluation_index_coverage_contract.py, a static regression-lock test with 0 DB/network dependency that fails if any of the 4 relevant indexes is ever dropped or the stale comment text ever reappears, (3) corrected this registry record's closure_criteria to reflect what was actually found rather than leaving factually-superseded wording in place. No migration was written -- this is the correct outcome, not a shortcut: the original 'migration needed' premise was itself unverified when the item was first triaged, and this wave supplied the verification. closure_commit is intentionally null rather than guessed, per this registry's established policy (see TD-CAND-001/002/003/007): a commit's SHA cannot be known before the commit object exists. remote_verified remains false: this closure has not yet been pushed or remotely CI-attested at the time of this registry edit.

items.title: Unconfirmed possible-secret heuristic hits from the secret-repo gate's warning tier
items.severity_reasoning: Not a security risk: the gate's blocking tier (finding_count) has been independently re-verified as 0 across many separate runs this session, including immediately before this classification pass -- the actual enforced security control is stable and reliable. The debt here is confined to the WARNING tier's own non-deterministic count, which is a tooling-quality/review-friction concern (a reviewer sees a fluctuating advisory number and may waste time investigating it) inside a script (scripts/quality/bys360_secret_repo_gate.py), not a runtime or production code path -- matches the P3 bar ('failure mode is review friction, not wrong behavior') even though the file itself is not literally under tests/scripts/docs the way the P3 anchor examples are.
items.description: The secret-repo gate's WARNING tier (secret_reference_or_placeholder / database_url_reference_or_placeholder -- not the blocking finding_count, which is 0) reported a non-deterministic count across different runs during this registry's authoring (77, 80, and 81 have all been observed on different invocations). The underlying report file is gitignored and regenerates on every run; this is advisory, heuristic, pattern-based signal, not a confirmed secret leak.
evidence: scripts/quality/bys360_secret_repo_gate.py (warning-tier classification logic)
reports/quality/BYS360_SECRET_REPO_GATE_V1_REPORT.json (gitignored, non-deterministic count across runs)
2026-08-19 re-verification: finding_count=0, warning_count=80 (within the previously-observed 77-81 range) -- blocking tier reliable, warning tier still non-deterministic

2026-08-20 root-cause forensic: 10 consecutive clean invocations of scripts/quality/bys360_secret_repo_gate.py against the unchanged repository all reported warning_count=80, and a diagnostic re-run of the exact same scan logic WITHOUT the add_warning() 80-item cap produced byte-identical output across 2 independent runs (194 true warnings both times) -- proving the underlying git-based candidate collection and scan (collect_repository_candidate_files + scan_file) was ALREADY fully deterministic given a fixed working tree; there was no traversal-order, dedup, path-normalization, or encoding nondeterminism anywhere in the mechanism

2026-08-20 root cause identified: add_warning(warnings, item, limit=80) in scripts/quality/bys360_secret_repo_gate.py silently stopped recording warnings once the list reached 80 entries, and warning_count_real = len(warnings) was computed AFTER that cap had already applied -- so the reported warning_count could mathematically never exceed 80 once the true match count grew past it, freezing the number at exactly 80 regardless of how much the real underlying signal changed. The historical 77/80/81 readings were not scan-time randomness: 77 reflected a genuine below-cap true count at an earlier point in the repository's growth; 80 is the cap's ceiling, hit consistently once true content crossed it; 81 predates the current cap value and is not reproducible under the present code.

2026-08-20 fix: add_warning() no longer caps recording; the true total (len(warnings), now genuinely unbounded) is always reported as warning_count. Only the DISPLAYED warning-detail list in the JSON report is truncated (at 80 entries, unchanged readability behavior) with an explicit truncation-marker entry stating the true total. finding_count and all blocking/allowlist/ignore logic are completely untouched -- zero security-policy diff.

2026-08-20 post-fix verification: warning_count now reports 194 (true total) against the pre-fix repository state, verified identical across 20 consecutive clean invocations (stdout byte-identical via `sort -u` collapsing to one line set); after adding this closure's own 4 new regression tests (which legitimately add more SECRET_KEY="changeme"-shaped fixture lines to tests/quality/test_bys360_secret_repo_gate.py, itself a scanned file), the count correctly and traceably rose to 201 (+7, exactly matching the +7 new warnings attributed to that one file in a per-path breakdown) -- proof the number now accurately tracks real content instead of being frozen behind a mask

2026-08-20 regression suite: 4 new tests added (test_warning_count_reports_true_total_not_capped_at_display_limit, test_warning_count_at_or_below_display_limit_has_no_truncation_marker, test_repeated_scan_is_semantically_deterministic [10 repeated invocations, full findings/warnings content equality, not just counts], test_scan_result_independent_of_git_add_commit_order [proves git ls-files' stable sort makes the result order-independent of commit order]); all 70 non-skipped tests in tests/quality/test_bys360_secret_repo_gate.py pass, including every pre-existing blocking-secret/allowlist/dedup test (test_tracked_real_secret_triggers_red, test_api_key_like_value_triggers_red, test_flask_secret_*_triggers_red, test_duplicate_path_across_lists_is_scanned_once, test_env_templates_are_allowed_but_runtime_env_files_are_blocked, etc.) -- proving no security weakening
items.closure_reason: Root-caused and fixed the secret-repo gate's warning-tier nondeterminism. The underlying git-based scan (collect_repository_candidate_files + scan_file) was already fully deterministic given a fixed working tree -- proven by byte-identical uncapped diagnostic output across independent runs. The actual defect was in add_warning()'s silent 80-item recording cap: warning_count_real was computed AFTER that cap already applied, so the reported number could never exceed 80 once the true match count grew past it, freezing the count at a masked ceiling instead of reflecting reality (explaining the historical 77/80/81 readings as genuine content-growth crossing near/past that ceiling over time, not per-invocation randomness). Fix: add_warning() now always records; only the report's DISPLAYED warning-detail list is truncated for readability (unchanged 80-entry limit, with an explicit truncation marker stating the true total), while warning_count itself is always the true, unbounded total. finding_count and every blocking/allowlist/ignore rule are completely untouched -- POLICY_DIFF = 0, confirmed by all pre-existing blocking-secret and allowlist tests continuing to pass unchanged. Post-fix: 20 consecutive runs against the unchanged repository are stdout-byte-identical; the count then correctly rose (194 -> 201) in direct, traceable response to this closure's own added test fixtures, proving the metric now genuinely tracks content rather than being frozen behind a mask. closure_commit is intentionally null rather than guessed, per this registry's established policy (see TD-CAND-001/TD-CAND-002): a commit's SHA cannot be known before the commit object exists. remote_verified remains false: this fix has not yet been pushed or remotely CI-attested at the time of this registry edit.

legacy_mapping.note: The underlying signal is itself non-deterministic/heuristic, so it cannot be matched to a specific legacy entry with any confidence.

closure_criteria: Root cause of the warning-tier count's run-to-run variance identified (e.g., filesystem iteration order, a timing-dependent generated file being scanned inconsistently).
Either the variance is fixed (deterministic warning count across runs), or it is documented as expected/inherent behavior of the heuristic with an explicit rationale -- not left unexplained.
The blocking finding_count mechanism remains untouched and still reliably 0 throughout.

behavior_quirks_to_preserve: The blocking finding_count=0 behavior must not change while investigating the warning-tier variance.

items.notes: Explicitly recorded as advisory/non-deterministic rather than a fixed fact -- do not cite a specific hit count from this item as authoritative; re-run the gate for a current count. finding_count (the blocking tier) is separately and reliably 0.
